charts.short: Per capita consumption of meat worldwide 2020-2032, by region
charts.description: The per capita consumption of meat was highest in North America, at roughly 78.6 kilos per person in the period between 2020 and 2022. By comparison, the average person living in Africa consumed about 9.6 kilos per year during that period.

charts.short: Market volume share of the global dairy products in 2023, by region
charts.description: This statistic shows the distribution of the dairy products market volume worldwide in 2023, by region. In that year, North America accounted for 14 percent of the dairy products worldwide export share, and EU-27 held 39 percent of the market.

charts.title: Share of people who follow a halal diet worldwide as of 2017 to 2021, by region
charts.short: Share of halal diet followers worldwide by region 2017-2021
charts.description: As of 2021, almost 48 percent of the population in the Middle East and Africa follow a halal diet. This includes avoiding the consumption of pork, blood and other meat which as not slaughtered according the Islamic guidelines. Furthermore it includes to avoid ingredients such as alcohol which are not conform with their religious beliefs.
charts.note: Worldwide; 2021

charts.title: Prevalence of severe food insecurity in the Asia-Pacific region in 2022, by region
charts.short: Prevalence of severe food insecurity APAC 2022, by region
charts.description: In 2022, approximately 19.4 percent of the population in South Asia were subject to severe food insecurity. Comparatively, the prevalence of severe food insecurity in East Asia amounted to around one percent that year.
charts.note: Asia, APAC; 2022

charts.title: Prevalence of severe food insecurity in East Asia from 2014 to 2022
charts.short: Prevalence of severe food insecurity East Asia 2014-2022
charts.description: In 2022, approximately one percent of the population in East Asia were subject to severe food insecurity. The share of population in severe food insecurity stayed consistent in East Asia compared to the previous year.
charts.note: Asia; 2014 to 2022

charts.title: Prevalence of severe food insecurity in Southeast Asia from 2014 to 2022
charts.short: Prevalence of severe food insecurity SEA 2014-2022
charts.description: In 2022, approximately 2.6 percent of the population in Southeast Asia were exposed to severe food insecurity. This was an increase from 2019, when around 1.8 percent of Southeast Asia's population were subject to severe food insecurity.
charts.note: Asia; 2014 to 2022

charts.title: Prevalence of severe food insecurity in South Asia from 2014 to 2022
charts.short: Prevalence of severe food insecurity South Asia 2014-2022
charts.description: In 2022, 19.4 percent of the population in South Asia was exposed to severe food insecurity. This was a decrease from the previous year, when around 21 percent of South Asia's population was subject to severe food insecurity.
charts.note: Asia; 2014 to 2022

charts.title: Share of low birth weight babies in the Asia-Pacific region in 2020, by country
charts.short: Share of low birth weight babies APAC 2020, by country
charts.description: In 2020, the share of low birth weight babies in India accounted for 27.44 percent, the highest share across the Asia-Pacific region, followed by Bangladesh and the Philippines. Newborns weighing less than 2.5 thousand grams are classified as low weight.
charts.note: Asia, APAC; 2020

charts.title: Disability-adjusted life years (DALY) rate for child and maternal malnutrition (CMM) in the Asia-Pacific region in 1990 and 2019, by subregion (per 100,000)
charts.short: DALY rate for child and maternal malnutrition APAC 1990-2019, by subregion
charts.description: In 2019, the disability-adjusted life years (DALY) rate for child and maternal malnutrition (CMM) in South Asia amounted to an estimated 6,323 per 100 thousand population, the highest across the Asia-Pacific region. Oceania followed with a CMM DALY count of around 5,401 per 100 thousand that year.
charts.note: Asia, Australia and Oceania, APAC; 1990 and 2019; age-standardized rates

charts.title: Death rate due to child and maternal malnutrition (CMM) in the Asia-Pacific region in 1990 and 2019, by subregion (per 100,000)
charts.short: Death rate due to child and maternal malnutrition APAC 1990-2019, by subregion
charts.description: In 2019, the death rate due to child and maternal malnutrition (CMM) in South Asia amounted to approximately 59 per 100 thousand population, the highest across the Asia-Pacific region. Oceania followed with a CMM death rate of around 57.7 per 100 thousand that year.
charts.note: Asia, Australia and Oceania, APAC; 1990 and 2019; age-standardized rates

charts.title: Share of population who are undernourished in Southeast Asia from 2015 to 2019, with forecasts to 2022
charts.short: Share of population who are undernourished SEA 2015-2022
charts.description: For 2022, it was forecast that five percent of the population in Southeast Asia would be undernourished. This would mark a decrease from 2015, when 7.5 percent of the population in SEA were undernourished.

charts.short: Number of undernourished people SEA 2015-2022
charts.description: In 2022, an estimated 34.1 million people in Southeast Asia were undernourished. This was a decrease from 2015, when approximately 47.9 million people across Southeast Asia were undernourished.

charts.title: Share of population who are undernourished in South Asia from 2015 to 2019, with forecasts to 2022
charts.short: Share of population who are undernourished South Asia 2015-2022

charts.title: Projected share of adults with obesity in the Asia-Pacific region in 2035, by country or territory
charts.short: Projected share of obese adults APAC 2035, by country
charts.description: The share of obese adults in New Zealand was projected to account for 49 percent of the country's population by 2035. Singapore, Japan, and Vietnam were projected to have the lowest obesity rates in the Asia-Pacific region, with obese adults in each of the countries set to account for less than ten percent of their total populations in 2035.
charts.note: Asia, APAC; 2022
charts.source: World Obesity Federation Share of population

charts.title: Compound annual growth rate of adult obesity in the Asia-Pacific region between 2020 and 2035, by country or territory
charts.short: CAGR of adult obesity APAC 2020-2035, by country
charts.description: Between 2020 and 2035, the adult obese population in Vietnam was projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 6.3 percent, the highest across the Asia-Pacific region. At the same time, the country was projected to have the lowest share of obese adults across the region by 2035.
charts.note: Asia, APAC; 2020 to 2035
charts.source: World Obesity Federation Share of population

charts.title: Estimated share of overweight children in the Asia-Pacific region in 2020, by country
charts.short: Share of overweight children APAC 2020, by country
charts.description: In 2020, approximately 18.5 percent of the children aged up to five years old in Australia were considered overweight. In contrast, 1.3 percent of the children under five years old in Sri Lanka were classified as overweight that year.
charts.note: Asia, APAC; 2020; among children under 5 years old

charts.title: Compound annual growth rate of child obesity in the Asia-Pacific region between 2020 and 2035, by country or territory
charts.short: CAGR of child obesity APAC 2020-2035, by country
charts.description: Between 2020 and 2035, the population of obese children in Vietnam was projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 9.8 percent, the highest across the Asia-Pacific region. In contrast, the CAGR for child obesity in Singapore between 2020 and 2035 was projected to be 0.8 percent.
charts.note: Asia, APAC; 2020 to 2035

charts.title: Share of population with diabetes in the Asia-Pacific region in 2021, by country
charts.short: Share of population with diabetes APAC 2021, by country
charts.description: In 2021, close to 31 percent of the population in Pakistan had diabetes. In comparison, Vietnam had the lowest prevalence of diabetic people across the Asia-Pacific region that year, approximately six percent.
charts.note: Asia, APAC; 2021; 20-79 years

charts.title: Disability-adjusted life years (DALY) rate for diabetes in the Asia-Pacific region in 2021, by country or territory (per 100,000)
charts.short: Disability-adjusted life years rate for diabetes APAC 2021, by country
charts.description: In 2021, the total disability-adjusted life years (DALY) for diabetes in Papua New Guinea amounted to an estimated 3,062 per 100 thousand population, the highest across the Asia-Pacific region. Brunei followed with a diabetes DALY count of around 2,279 per 100 thousand that year.

charts.title: Share of adults with hypertension in the Asia-Pacific region in 2019, by country
charts.short: Prevalence of high blood pressure among adults APAC 2019, by country
charts.description: In 2019, Brunei had the highest share of adults with hypertension in the Asia-Pacific region, approximately 46.4 percent. In contrast, the share of adults with high blood pressure in Cambodia amounted to around 25.7 percent.

This marked a significant increase from around three million dollars privately invested in the region's alternative protein industry in 2016 and 2017, respectively.
